body:
After Kishkindha Kaandam, Dinjith Ayyathan returns to the thriller genre with Eko, a suspense film that remains deeply rooted and realistic in its treatment. The film keeps you guessing the motives and loyalties of its characters until the very end.

The screenplay is extremely tight, with hardly any scenes that do not contribute directly to the gradual revelation of the mystery. Even those scenes serve an important purpose from a character-building perspective. The detailing in the dialogues keeps you alert, urging you to constantly track the information revealed so far and understand how new details fit into the larger picture.

Yet the film's pacing remains grounded and natural. The scenes do not feel engineered solely to reveal information to the audience. Instead, they unfold organically, with revelations emerging as a by-product of events that seem to occur realistically within the world of the film.

Perhaps intentionally, the interpersonal relationships between the characters are not fully revealed. Due to this, the viewer is not able to fully understand the reasons for the loyalties and actions of the characters.

As with many Malayalam films, the serene natural beauty of lush green forests and hills, along with the characters' backgrounds and the timeline, all add to the rootedness of the narrative. The setting feels inseparable from the story, as if it could belong only to this region and time.

When it comes to performances, there are no weak links. Every actor delivers a restrained and authentic performance.

Standing out among them is Sandeep Pradeep, who excels with a finely nuanced portrayal of the many shades of Peeyos' character. Saurabh Sachdeva, being the accomplished actor he is, appears somewhat underutilized, as his character remains largely an enigma for most of the film. Even so, he has some powerful moments where he brings complete honesty to the screen.

In the end, Eko leaves you in awe not only because of the revelations, but also because of the finesse with which the thriller is crafted, remaining grounded and realistic while being consistently engaging.

What a Fab movie - EKO!! Start to end - didn't miss a beat. Watched it twice, and absolutely enjoyed the second Watch as much as the first. Every bit in this movie meant something and all characters were on point and dialogues were so well written. Cinematography is brilliant as well.

Can't stop loving Malayalam movies!!!

Eko is a rare slow-burn thriller that asks the audience for patience and rewards it with a deeply satisfying conclusion. The narrative unfolds quietly, building tension through silence, atmosphere, and subtle detail rather than conventional twists.

The cinematography is outstanding every frame feels alive. The color grading leans heavily into lush greens and cool natural tones, almost letting the forest swallow the characters. The visual texture makes nature feel like the central presence in the film, shaping mood and meaning without needing to speak.

The symbolic use of dogs is one of the film's most impressive choices. They operate as metaphors for loyalty, instinct, unpredictability, and the hidden wildness lying beneath human behavior. It's smart storytelling that deepens the mystery and emotional resonance.

There's a strong Korean-thriller influence in the pacing and tone: slow, tense, grounded in realism, and ending with a cathartic impact rather than loud spectacle. The final act ties everything together with clarity and weight, making the build-up feel absolutely worth it.

Eko may not appeal to those looking for fast action, but for viewers who enjoy atmospheric, layered films with meaningful visuals. It's a brilliant and memorable experience.

I rarely write reviews, but this film compelled me to. The screenplay is exceptional-layered, intelligent, and deeply engaging.

After Kishkinta Kaandam, the director takes a massive leap forward here. Every scene has purpose, every silence speaks, and the film fully trusts its audience.

As a Tamil viewer, this only reinforces how much Malayalam cinema prioritizes writing and honesty over formulas. Tamil filmmakers have a lot to learn here instead of endlessly chasing masala tropes and "mass" hero moments.

This isn't just a good Indian film-it's one of the best I've seen.

Eko caught me off guard in the best way.

I went in completely blind, with no expectations, and the film slowly pulled me into its quiet, unsettling mystery. It resists easy answers, letting mood and behaviour do most of the work, and that restraint really pays off. The tension holds steadily, without cheap scares or over-explaining what's going on.

The final act is where Eko truly lands its punch. The twist arrives suddenly and unexpectedly, forcing you to reassess much of what you've been watching.

Performances across the board are solid and understated, fitting the film's grounded tone even if no single role dominates.

The film isn't airtight - the middle section wanders at times, and a few narrative threads feel undercooked or loosely resolved. A tighter screenplay could have sharpened the overall impact.

Still, Eko succeeds as an atmospheric, engaging slow-burn mystery that rewards patience.

An unexpected and satisfying 7/10.
